research_problem: No systematic overview of GraphQL research despite growing industrial adoption as an alternative to REST
technical_approach: Systematic mapping study (Petersen/Kuhrmann) over 6 databases with search string 'graphql' (2015-June 2021) plus a conceptual framework of 17 GraphQL components
primary_contribution: First SMS of GraphQL: 84 primary studies classified by venue, research type, setting, SWEBOK area, contribution domain/type, components and frontiers
dataset_benchmark: 84 primary studies (3,185 -> 254 -> 135 -> 80 + 4 manual), incl. 30.95% gray literature (theses); supplementary dataset
key_findings: 61.91% validation/evaluation research but 71.43% academic, no government; only 4 testing studies and 4 client-only studies; directives, validation, subscriptions least studied; GraphQL faster/smaller for complex queries, slower for simple ones; 39.73% of 2,094 schemas have cycles; DoS, caching, mutation limitations; roadmap: industrial experiments, security/caching practices, testing, SLA and pricing
author_limitations: Manual classification may introduce selection errors; mitigated with decision tables, second-reviewer checks and consensus
analyst_limitations: Inconsistent growth figures (16.67%/13.61% vs 66%/98%); cut-off June 2021; single-term search; gray literature without quality appraisal; performance claims aggregated without appraisal; no inter-rater agreement
reproducibility: Supplementary datasets published; simple search string
suggested_extensions: GraphQL testing (transfer REST techniques), subscription testing, field-level authorization and cost-based DoS defence, cycle-aware generation, client-side/LLM query construction, updated rapid review post-2021
evidence_location: Funnel p.13; validity p.16-18; RQ3 p.21-22; RQ5 p.23; RQ6 p.24-27; RQ7 p.28-29; roadmap p.31
integrity: Tables 2,5-7,10 column-split; all figures missing; percentages recoverable from text
